reasoning: No hantavirus vaccine for humans has ever received full FDA approval, and none are in late-stage US clinical trials. Vaccine development from early research to approval typically takes 5–10 years; with only ~1.5 years remaining, and very low disease incidence complicating efficacy trials, the chance of full approval by end of 2026 is below 1%. The market's 8.5% implied probability is far too high.
evidence_points: No hantavirus vaccine is listed in the FDA’s approved vaccines or known to be in a Phase 3 trial targeting US licensure.
Hantavirus incidence in the US is extremely low (sporadic cases), making large-scale efficacy trials impractical without international collaboration, which is not underway for US approval.
Even accelerated approval pathways require substantial clinical data and a validated surrogate endpoint, none of which is publicly planned for hantavirus before 2026.
sources_consulted: FDA Vaccines Licensed for Use in the United States (fda.gov)
ClinicalTrials.gov search for hantavirus vaccine Phase 2/3
Published reviews on hantavirus vaccine development (WHO, PubMed)
